title: The cone-adjunction unit identifies weighted and section evaluation
statement:
Use simplicial sets, quasicategories, Kan complexes, internal functor simplicial sets and weak homotopy equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in universes containing all displayed constructions. Use the explicit enriched presheaf model, its simplicial unstraightening $U_K$ and ordinary cone adjunction $T\dashv U_K$ of [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation], and the ordered-subset realization of [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching]. Let $K$ be a small quasicategory, $A=\mathfrak C[K]^{\mathrm{op}}$, $z$ the last vertex of $K\star\Delta^0$, and $W(k)=\mathfrak C[K\star\Delta^0](k,z)=T(1_K)(k)$. Let $u:K\to U_KW$ be the ordinary adjunction unit. For an enriched functor $F:A\to\mathbf{Kan}_{\mathcal V}$ put $L=\underline{\operatorname{Nat}}(W,F)$, with mapping simplicial sets as in [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation]. The simplicial map
$$c_F:L\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}_{/K}(K,U_KF),\qquad c_F(\ell)=U_K(\ell)u,$$
identifies the section-evaluation cone after precomposition by $c_F$ with the weighted cone $W(k)\times L\to F(k)$, via the natural fibre comparisons and the transpose $m_F$ of $F$. Here the weighted cone means the coherent join cone obtained from the enriched functor on the collage with new first vertex $L$ and morphism weights $W$, as in [lem-coef-coherent-weight-limit-recognition]; use [lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus] to read it as a coherent transformation. This is an identification of full coherent cones, including all simplicial parameters. Explicitly, over $\sigma:\Delta^r\to K$, the section associated to $\ell:W\times\Delta^n\to F$ is represented by $T_\sigma\times\Delta^n\to W\times\Delta^n\xrightarrow{\ell}F$. The map $T_\sigma\to W$ takes each direct generator and each subset labeling its factorization to the same generator or subset in the ordered cone. Evaluation at $k$ is therefore $\ell_k$ on the direct edge $k\to z$, and all transport homotopies and iterated coherences are those of weighted evaluation. These identifications commute with every base-simplex and parameter-simplex operator, and with enriched natural transformations of $F$.

source.place: Returned Step 11, unit/generator comparison of the two cones; HTT 2.2.1–2.2.3 and 3.3.3.4 Argument extracted from the returned proof; HTT supplies the background constructions, not a verbatim assertion of this formulated lemma. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical comparison.

proof.text:
Set up the actual evaluation. By [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation], $T$ is left Quillen and every slice object is cofibrant. Thus $W=T(1_K)$ is projectively cofibrant. Since $F$ is objectwise Kan, the simplicial model axiom applied to $\varnothing\to W$ and $F\to *$ makes $L=\underline{\operatorname{Nat}}(W,F)$ Kan. Hence $L$ is an object of $\mathbf{Kan}_{\mathcal V}$, not merely a simplicial set of vertices. Define $m_F$ by transposing $F$ along $\mathfrak C[K^{\mathrm{op}}]\cong\mathfrak C[K]^{\mathrm{op}}$ into $\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$ as in [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces]. Define $e_k:W(k)\times L\to F(k)$ by $e_k(w,\ell)=\ell_k(w)$ in every simplicial degree. Enriched naturality says, for $a\in\mathfrak C[K](k,l)$,
$$e_k(w\circ a,\ell)=F(a)e_l(w,\ell).$$
Together with identities and associativity, this is precisely the enriched functor on the reversed ordered cone, with new first object $L$, used to define the weighted join cone in [lem-coef-coherent-weight-limit-recognition]. No limit-recognition conclusion is used here.

source.place: Sections 2.2.1 and 2.2.3 (projective presentation); weighted evaluation is defined directly; agent-written unit/evaluation calculation, not a verbatim theorem of HTT. No Stacks tag states this comparison.

proof.text: Compute the unit on each simplex using the ordinary adjunction of [lem-coef-cone-presheaf-adjunction]. For $\sigma:\Delta^r\to K$, let $i_\sigma=T(\sigma):T_\sigma\to T(1_K)=W$. Under the adjunction, the unit $u:K\to U_KW$ corresponds to $1_W$. Restricting its adjoint family to $\sigma$ therefore gives $1_Wi_\sigma=i_\sigma$. This proves that $u(\sigma)$ is the actual natural map $i_\sigma$, with no fibrant replacement of $W$. In the pushout defining $T_\sigma$, the functor inducing $i_\sigma$ is $\mathfrak C[\sigma\star1]$ on the cone and the identity on $\mathfrak C[K]$. The common face agrees, so the functor exists by the pushout property. It fixes the cone vertex and sends a subset-labelled cone arrow to its image in the same ordered cone, by [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching]. Consequently both direct cone arrows and their entire factorization simplices have the claimed images.

source.place: Section 2.2.1, cone pushout and ordinary adjunction; agent-written unit/evaluation calculation, not a verbatim theorem of HTT. No Stacks tag states this comparison.

proof.text:
Keep track of the enrichment, rather than treating $T\dashv U_K$ as a simplicial adjunction. Let $\pi_r:Q^r\to\Delta^r$ be the maximum-subset map of [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching]. Collapsing the whole base of the cone of $\sigma$ to one object induces a map $\rho_{\sigma,k}:T_\sigma(k)\to Q^r$, natural in $k$; the defining pushout maps to $\mathfrak C[J^r]$ because the initial $\Delta^r$ has become constant. The canonical enrichment of $U_K$ specified in [lem-coef-unstraightening-homotopy-descent] is induced by these maps $Q^r\to\Delta^r$. Thus for $\ell:W\times\Delta^n\to F$, the map $c_F(\ell):K\times\Delta^n\to U_KF$ takes an $r$-simplex $(\sigma,\theta)$, where $\theta:\Delta^r\to\Delta^n$, to the natural map with components
$$t\longmapsto\ell_k\bigl(i_{\sigma,k}(t),\theta\pi_r\rho_{\sigma,k}(t)\bigr).$$
Indeed the first coordinate is the unit family of Step 2, while the second is exactly the parameter map used by the specified enrichment before applying $U_K(\ell)$. Only the enrichment clause of the cited descent node is used; its Dwyer--Kan assertion for bifibrant diagrams is not applied to $W$. This is the precise simplexwise interpretation of the parameterized map $T_\sigma\times\Delta^n\to W\times\Delta^n\to F$ in the statement.

source.place: Section 2.2.2, maximum-subset map and the parameter map in unstraightening; agent-written unit/evaluation calculation, not a verbatim theorem of HTT. No Stacks tag states this comparison.

proof.text:
Check all operators explicitly. For $\alpha:[s]\to[r]$, the induced $T_\alpha:T_{\sigma\alpha}\to T_\sigma$ satisfies
$$i_\sigma T_\alpha=i_{\sigma\alpha},\qquad
\rho_\sigma T_\alpha=Q(\alpha)\rho_{\sigma\alpha},\qquad
\pi_r Q(\alpha)=\Delta(\alpha)\pi_s.$$
The first two identities are the two composites of the same maps on the defining pushout; the last is $\max\alpha(I)=\alpha(\max I)$, also for noninjective $\alpha$. Substituting them into Step 3 gives exactly its formula for $(\sigma\alpha,\theta\alpha)$. A parameter operator $\beta:[m]\to[n]$ replaces $\ell$ by $\ell(1\times\beta)$, so both sides replace $\theta$ by $\beta\theta$. For an enriched natural map $b:F\to G$, both sides postcompose the displayed value with $b_k$. These equalities prove faces, degeneracies and naturality in $F$ for every degree, rather than just on the vertices of $L$. They also show directly that the formula defines the simplicial map $c_F$.

source.place: Sections 2.2.1-2.2.2, functoriality of cone pushouts and maximum-subset maps; agent-written unit/evaluation calculation, not a verbatim theorem of HTT. No Stacks tag states this comparison.

proof.text:
Compare vertex evaluation with the specified fibre comparison. Over a vertex $k$, the unit $u(k)$ is the natural map from the representable $T_k$ to $W$ determined by the direct arrow $e_k^0:k\to z$ (Step 2). The parameter construction in Step 3 on the constant base simplex is the canonical map $j_{F(k)}:F(k)\to(U_KF)_k$ induced by $Q^r\to\Delta^r$. Therefore the entire vertex evaluation map $L\to(U_KF)_k$ of $c_F$ is
$$j_{F(k)}\circ\bigl(\ell\longmapsto\ell_k(e_k^0)\bigr).$$
The fibre comparison is a weak equivalence by [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation]. Thus evaluation is $e_k$ on the direct cone edge under that comparison; an inverse to $j_{F(k)}$ is neither asserted to be a strict simplicial inverse nor used to define $c_F$. For $K=\Delta^0$, this specializes to $W=\Delta^0$, $L=F(k)$ and $c_F=j_{F(k)}$, which also checks the direction of the comparison.

source.place: Section 2.2.2, Remark 2.2.2.11 and the maximum-subset fibre comparison; agent-written unit/evaluation calculation, not a verbatim theorem of HTT. No Stacks tag states this comparison.

proof.text: Compare the coherences on a base simplex, not only its vertex values. In $\mathfrak C[\Delta^r\star\Delta^0](i,z)$ a simplex is a chain $I_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq I_d$ of subsets containing $i,z$. Its image in $W(\sigma(i))$ under Step 2 is that same chain mapped by $\sigma\star1$. A face deletes an $I_j$, a degeneracy repeats it, and composing a base arrow with a cone arrow takes union of their subsets, by [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching]. Applying $e_{\sigma(i)}$ to these images gives the weighted cone's homotopies. By the displayed enriched naturality equation in Step 1, union with a base arrow gives exactly the $F$-action on the value at its other endpoint. Step 3 applies $\ell$ to exactly these same images, with the same parameter coordinate. Thus the direct value, each homotopy and every iterated union-composition coherence agree. For general $K$, this calculation descends through the simplex-colimit relations defining $\mathfrak C[K]$: Step 4 proves compatibility for every simplex map, so two representatives related by those relations have the same image. No claim that direct edges alone determine a coherent cone is needed.

source.place: Section 2.2.1 and ordered-subset rigidification: direct calculation on every chain; agent-written unit/evaluation calculation, not a verbatim theorem of HTT. No Stacks tag states this comparison.

proof.text: Use [lem-coef-unstraightening-simplex-transport] with this objectwise Kan $F$. Its simplex formula identifies the vertex restrictions, subset-generator homotopies and union-composition coherences of $T_\sigma\to F$ with the actual fibre-transport functor $m_F$, naturally in all extra simplicial parameters. Applying that assertion to the family in Step 3 reads precisely the data computed in Steps 5-6 as the section-evaluation cone precomposed with $c_F$. The same data, read as the enriched functor on the collage with vertex $L$, are the weighted join cone of Step 1. Hence the identification is of the full coherent cones over $m_F$ with the same apex; it is not inferred from equality of the vertex maps. Finally use the fixed-boundary, fixed-vertex comparison of [lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus] to express this join-cone identification in the coherent-transformation convention. That comparison preserves the apex and boundary diagram. Step 4 and the additional-parameter clause of the transport node show that the resulting cone identification commutes with every base and parameter operator and with every enriched natural transformation of $F$.
